result.question: How does Nvidia characterize the impact of export controls on its business with China?
result.answer: Nvidia characterizes the impact of U.S. export controls on its China business as broadly negative and potentially escalating. The company states that its competitive position "has been harmed" by existing export controls and that future results "may be further harmed" if there are further changes to the rules [c0001045810-25-000023:item-1-p016]. Nvidia warns that changes to export controls could subject a wider range of its products to restrictions and licensing requirements, "negatively impacting our business and financial results" [c0001045810-25-000023:item-1a-p035]. In the event of such changes, Nvidia says it may be unable to sell its inventory of affected products and may be unable to develop replacement products not subject to licensing, "effectively excluding us from all or part of the China market," as well as other impacted markets including the Middle East and countries designated "Tier 2" by the AI Diffusion IFR [c0001045810-25-000023:item-1a-p035]. Nvidia also notes that export controls may disrupt its supply and distribution chain for a substantial portion of its products, which are warehoused in and distributed from Hong Kong [c0001045810-25-000023:item-1a-p035]. Beyond China, Nvidia states that "excessive or shifting export controls" have already encouraged customers outside China to "design-out" U.S. semiconductors and have encouraged overseas governments to request that customers purchase from competitors rather than Nvidia, harming its business, market position, and financial results [c0001045810-25-000023:item-1a-p035]. The company further warns that export controls may negatively impact demand for its products and services not only in China but also in other markets such as Europe, Latin America, and Southeast Asia [c0001045810-25-000209:part-ii--item-1a-p012]. Nvidia also highlights that export controls increase the risk of investing in U.S. advanced semiconductor products, because by the time a new product reaches market it may be subject to new controls, "resulting in excess inventory and purchase obligations as we recently experienced with the H20" [c0001045810-25-000209:part-ii--item-1a-p012]. Additionally, Nvidia notes that any new control impacting a wider range of its products would "likely have a disproportionate impact on NVIDIA" and may disadvantage it against competitors selling chips outside the scope of such controls [c0001045810-25-000023:item-1a-p035].
